newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CLABECQ UNIONS ASK WORKERS TO REJECT OFFER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CLABECQ UNIONS ASK WORKERS TO REJECT OFFER.

text.p: Trade unionists at bankrupt Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq, which is being considered for a takeover, on Saturday urged workers taking part in a referendum next week to say "no" to an early retirement offer.

Clabecq's 1,800 workers have already rejected a proposal which the Walloon Region, the firm's majority-shareholder, drew up last month following talks with unions, court-appointed receivers and federal ministers.

But the socialist FGTB union's moderate president, Michel Nollet, has sinced intervened and obtained clarifications on the proposal which covers early retirement, the problem of workers over 50 and the allocation of money made on the sale of stock.

Union representatives at Clabecq agreed this week to a referendum on May 6, but told a general assembly of workers on Saturday the package still offered no guarantees for the future and that they should reject it.

"The text (being put forward) contains early retirement pensions which are the lowest among steel makers in our country....," Roberto D'Orazio, the militant socialist trade union leader at Clabecq, told Belgian television.
The plan aims to alleviate the consequences of bankruptcy for the workers and make the company attractive for a takeover.
Several firms have been mentioned as possible buyers, but the only one to have publicly declared an interest is private Italian-Swiss steel and commodity trader Duferco.
There have been a number of clashes between police and the steelworkers since Clabecq, based in the small town of Tubize near Brussels, was declared bankrupt in January.
However, a "decisive" demonstration which had previously been announced for Saturday did not take place.
